one_line: Live Go JD: must-haves are production Go, testing, CI/CD, observability — domain never a requirement; no portfolio link requested
Canonical hiring-guide: code output works at top of funnel then dive-deeper on 1-2 projects; published projects matter most for students/nontraditional

column10: Atlassian reads take-homes for: runs? tests? requirements? sane tech? — warns against 'odd or shiny things in order to impress us'

one_line: n=13,732 survey: relevant real-world assessments are tech leaders' #1 concern; senior hiring +19-22% vs entry +7%
Hiring practitioners split on repo-checking; code checks 'mostly for junior-level'; link directly to PRs/pinned repos not bare profile
Official Go definition of competence = conformance to shared idioms (gofmt, naming, errors, defer) — mechanically checkable, domain-independent
Go team n=11,840: new Gophers disproportionately lack concurrency guidance; all levels lack project-layout guidance; API/RPC + CLI are top uses
Wheel-project pedagogy (Redis/Git/Docker/SQLite in Go) exercises concurrency/B-trees; spec-compatibility is the anti-fake verifiable claim
Community: 'small and complete... finishing the whole arc, not scale'; difficulty estimates Redis 20-40h, RAFT 40-80h, SQLite 60-120h; listicles = 'recommendation porn'
556k-star community canon of rebuild-from-scratch projects; Go sections = database/Redis, container, load balancer, CLI — level-graded from 100-line tools to B+tree DBs
167 exercises / 35 concepts tree-structured by dependency; official GoBridge/GDN mentoring platform — the fundamentals layer before portfolio work
TDD-first curriculum with explicit order: interfaces -> errors -> DI/mocking -> concurrency -> sync -> context -> generics -> net/http application capstone
Clearest concept-to-project-type mapping: quiz CLI (goroutines/channels) -> URL shortener (handlers/middleware) -> Blackjack AI (interfaces) -> Quiet HN (concurrency/race)
One start-to-finish production net/http app (stdlib-only) as vehicle for project structure, SQL, sessions, security, testing — depth of one real app over breadth of toys
Staged order: guided projects first, then first personal 20-40h project deliberately NOT for the resume; commit often, README, avoid thin library wrappers
Steel-manned contrarian: GitHub is a noisy unscalable signal — forked tutorials and abandoned repos create visual activity without evidence (vendor-motivated)
GitHub Archive analysis: 83% of users zero commits/year; Dan Luu saw code examined in 2 of 50 interviews; 190k repos named 'datasciencecoursera'
When reviewers look they read merged PRs surviving someone else's review — red flags: oversized diffs, months-open PRs, typo-spray, unnarratable merges
